claim.pdf_says: 9.1.18.5   Run unit termination ... 9.1.18.6   Object orientation ... 9.1.18.7   Exception conditions  (fourth-level subclauses of 9.1.18 Commit and Rollback, peers of 9.1.18.1 through 9.1.18.4)
claim.markdown_says: ## 9.1.18.5 Run unit termination ... ## 9.1.18.6 Object orientation ... ## 9.1.18.7 Exception conditions  (whereas ISO_COBOL.md has '## 9.1.18 Commit and Rollback', '### 9.1.18.1 General', '### 9.1.18.2 Files and data items to be included', '### 9.1.18.3 Committing changes to files', '### 9.1.18.4 Rolling back changes to files and data items')
claim.why_it_matters: The last three subclauses of the Commit and Rollback clause are emitted at the same level as the clause itself, so an outline shows 9.1.18 as containing only .1 to .4 and lists .5, .6, .7 as sibling clauses. Heading text, numbers and anchors are correct; nothing normative is lost.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed on both sides, and the claim's quotations of both sources are exact. PDF page 264 (printed folio 234) renders, in ISO's bold serif run-in heading style: '9.1.18.5   Run unit termination', '9.1.18.6   Object orientation', '9.1.18.7   Exception conditions', then '9.1.19   Sort file' and '9.1.20   Merge file'. ISO does not visually distinguish third- from fourth-level headings, so the printed clause NUMBER is the sole carrier of depth, and 9.1.18.5/.6/.7 are unambiguously fourth-level subclauses of 9.1.18. In specs/ISO_COBOL.md the parent is '## 9.1.18 Commit and Rollback' (line 11602) with children '### 9.1.18.1' (11605), '### 9.1.18.2' (11610), '### 9.1.18.3' (11615), '### 9.1.18.4' (11620), but '## 9.1.18.5' (11633), '## 9.1.18.6' (11638) and '## 9.1.18.7' (11643) are level 2 -- peers of their own parent and of '## 9.1.19 Sort file' (11650). This is an internal contradiction inside one clause, not an alternate convention: across the whole file, four-part x.y.z.w numbers are level 3 in 620 cases versus 162 at level 2 and 24 at level 4, and .1-.4 of this very clause use level 3. Refutation was attempted on every available ground and failed: no text is missing or reflowed away (all three heading strings and all four body paragraphs are present verbatim); it is not line wrapping or hyphenation; it is not page-break furniture in the exclusionary sense -- the page break at line 11626/11629 is the CAUSE, but the effect lands on real content (the clause hierarchy) rather than on a running header, folio or licence line, all of which are handled separately here. The defect is therefore genuine. It is correctly rated cosmetic: heading text, clause numbers and the '#section-9-1-18-5/6/7' anchors are all correct and no normative prose is lost. Its one practical consequence is that any heading-scoped extraction of section 9.1.18 terminates at .4 and silently drops run-unit termination, the object-orientation prohibition and the EC-FLOW-APPLY / EC-FLOW-COMMIT / EC-FLOW-ROLLBACK rules.
verdict.corrected_description: Real, but the 'missing-heading' label is wrong -- no heading is missing. All three headings (9.1.18.5 Run unit termination, 9.1.18.6 Object orientation, 9.1.18.7 Exception conditions) are present in specs/ISO_COBOL.md with correct text, correct clause numbers and correct anchors; their following paragraphs are complete and verbatim. The actual defect is a heading-LEVEL error (kind should be 'heading-level' / wrong nesting depth): lines 11633, 11638 and 11643 use '##' where their four sibling subclauses at lines 11605-11620 use '###' under the '## 9.1.18 Commit and Rollback' parent at line 11602, so the three tail subclauses become peers of their own parent and of '## 9.1.19 Sort file'. The trigger is the page 263->264 break immediately preceding 9.1.18.5. Not a one-off: the file contains 162 four-part clause numbers emitted at level 2 against 620 at level 3, of which 58 sit within eight lines of a 'Page N' marker -- so the transcription has a recurring heading-depth reset that is only partly page-break-driven and warrants a file-wide sweep rather than a single-line patch. Severity cosmetic is correct for prose fidelity; the only functional risk is heading-scoped section extraction of 9.1.18 truncating after .4.
